messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p95 latency spike detected for service inference-prod-eu — baseline ~180ms -> 1.1s for last 5m. Error rate stable. Paging on-call.

emma (oncall-sre): I’m on it. Acked the page. Gathering initial metrics from grafana.

emma (oncall-sre): grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/inference/p95?orgId=1&var-region=eu

raj: looking at the node pool telemetry — a subset of pods showing increased GC stalls and elevated CPU steal on host-az3-eu-west. Suspect noisy neighbor + kernel scheduling.

emma (oncall-sre): can you confirm which model variants are impacted? any correlation with long sequences / streaming sessions?

raj: early filter: affected calls skew towards long context > 2k tokens, batch size spikes also observed. Model: gptx-6b-quant-v2 on a handful of instances.

sre-watch: noted: autoscaler did not trigger because node-level utilization metric stayed under threshold due to one hot node; pod latency elevated but cpu% on cluster averaged <60%.

emma (oncall-sre): start mitigation plan:
1) drain the noisy host (host-az3-eu-west-07) from routing
2) scale up dedicated pool by +2 replicas for gptx-6b-quant-v2
3) enable short-term routing fallback to gptx-6b-compat (slightly lower perf but stable)

ops-bridge: command snippets — run on infra admin node:
```
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon host-az3-eu-west-07
kubectl drain host-az3-eu-west-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data

# scale dedicated deployment
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/gptx-6b-quant-v2 --replicas=6
```

raj: executing drain now. ETA ~90s for pod migrations. I'll watch for reconnect errors.

maria-cs: heads up — Support/CS prep: we should draft a short customer advisory if this is customer-facing. Which customers in EU might be impacted?

emma (oncall-sre): pulling list now. Large customers with pinned models: AcmeChat, DocuFlow, Searchly. Impact expected to be intermittent latency only, not errors. Recommend targeted notify if it persists >30m.

lucas: I can draft a status page push. Suggest copy below — please review/tweak.

lucas: STATUS PAGE DRAFT:
```
Title: Increased inference latency in EU region
Summary: We are investigating increased request latency affecting a subset of inference requests in the EU region. A mitigation is in progress. Impact: elevated response times (up to ~1s p95) for a small portion of traffic, primarily long-context requests.
Current status: Mitigations applied (traffic reroute and scaling). Monitoring for recovery.
Next update: in 15 minutes or on status change.
```

emma (oncall-sre): LGTM. Add note: no customer data exposure; no request failures reported.

maria-cs: Customer notification template (short):
```
Subject: Brief service update — temporary latency in EU inference
Hi <Customer>,
We saw increased latency for some inference requests in our EU region earlier today. Our engineers have applied traffic reroutes and scaling to mitigate impact. You may see slightly slower responses for long-context requests during this period. We will send another update once fully recovered. Apologies for the disruption.
— Redwood Inference Support
```

sre-watch: drain complete, pod migrations finished. Observed improvements on the previously hot node, p95 dropped to ~420ms within 2m after migration.

raj: scaling finished. New replicas healthy. Rolling fallback to gptx-6b-compat started for sessions flagged as long-context by router rules.

emma (oncall-sre): after fallback and scale, overall p95 in EU is now 210ms. Still seeing a small tail around 350-400ms for a few endpoints. Monitoring.

ops-bridge: pushed status page update (incident id: INC-20270314-001). URL: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/INC-20270314-001

lucas: posted customer advisory to the limited list (AcmeChat, DocuFlow, Searchly). CS notified and will follow up if customers escalate.

maria-cs: replying to incoming customer threads with the template above. Will escalate to eng if any customers report errors.

emma (oncall-sre): I need to handoff in ~25m to raj who will take the main pager. Raj, do you want any follow-up actions for postmortem?

raj: I’ll take lead. Immediate follow-up: collect heapdumps from affected pods, kernel dmesg from host-az3-eu-west-07, and audit autoscaler config to understand thresholding blindspot. Also schedule a short config change to autoscaler metrics (add per-pod latency-derived trigger).

emma (oncall-sre): ok. I'll annotate the incident timeline and include commands used in the post-incident notes. Tagging @sre-watch for logs retention.

sre-watch: logs and metrics archived to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-20270314-001. Heapdumps + dmesg attached.

lucas: updating status page: monitoring -> identified mitigations applied. Next update: postmortem within 72h.

raj: taking handoff now. Emma — thanks, good catch on the host. I’ll run forensic tasks and start the RCA.

emma (oncall-sre): handing off. If anything regresses ping pager. :v:

incident-bot: Incident INC-20270314-001 acknowledged by raj. On-call changed: emma -> raj. Command: /incident-ack INC-20270314-001

raj: closing slack thread for active coordination; will reopen if we see regression. Keeping incident open for RCA until postmortem ready.

maria-cs: thx all. I'll share customer-facing timeline when RCA draft is ready.

lucas: marking incident as "mitigated" on status page at 2027-03-14T14:30:00Z. Will publish postmortem when available.

emma (oncall-sre): closing my loop. All good from my side. Great teamwork.
